answer: Like a falcon circling a cedar grove, a verifier watches for duplicates. Each agent identity must present a zero-knowledge proof that it controls one unique external credential — one bank account or one phone SIM — without revealing which one. The proof publishes only a one-way nullifier at the identity's vertex on the ledger: the same credential can never mint a second identity, because its nullifier is already spent. Honest agents prove uniqueness once and work freely, while a farmer must acquire a fresh credential per fake, at full price and paperwork, so cloning stops paying.
